This page is a short map of the **business** side of the low-altitude economy (LAE).

- Firm lists stay on [Companies & sectors](landscape.qmd).
- Weekly tools stay on the week pages under **Teach** (for example [Week 1](week-01.qmd)).
- Definitions stay in the [Glossary](glossary.qmd).

## How value is created

LAE is a **system**, not only aircraft. The system includes craft, take-off and landing sites, digital traffic and coordination, operators, customers, and supporting services ([Week 1](week-01.qmd)).

A service creates **value** when it does at least one of these well:

- saves time;
- cuts cost or risk;
- improves access; or
- enables a mission that other modes cannot do well.

Still commercially hard without willingness to pay, real demand, utilization/load factor, and costs under control. Technology helps only when it improves <strong>full-service</strong> economics — not a flashy airframe alone.</p>

A service is still commercially hard unless customers are willing to pay, demand is real, aircraft and sites are used enough (**utilization** and **load factor**), and operating and investment costs stay under control.

Technology helps only when it improves the **economics of the full service** — not when it only makes the aircraft look advanced ([Week 1](week-01.qmd); [Week 3](week-03.qmd)).

In class, unit-cost language includes [CASK](glossary.qmd#business-and-economics) (**cost per available seat-kilometre** — cost of passenger capacity offered) and mission-based measures for cargo or public-service work ([Week 3](week-03.qmd); [Glossary](glossary.qmd#business-and-economics)).

## Value chain

This section names **roles** only — how value moves along the chain.

It does **not** give market sizes, deal values, or firm names.

Trial programmes help teams test under controlled conditions. They are **not** the same as everyday commercial approval ([Week 7](week-07.qmd)).

<div class="vchain-flow">

</div>
<p class="vchain-note">Based on Weeks 1–3, 5–7, and 12. Roles only — no firm names and no market-size (TAM/SAM) figures.</p>

## How sectors fit

[Companies & sectors](landscape.qmd) groups checked entries into eleven roles:

| Role on that page | What it usually contributes |
|-------------------|-----------------------------|
| Aircraft and airframe makers | Vehicles and platforms |
| Delivery and logistics | Cargo / last-mile style missions |
| Inspection and surveying | Asset and site inspection missions |
| Emergency and medical | Public-safety / medical transport trials |
| Tourism and entertainment | Visitor / show / attraction flights |
| eVTOL and passenger trials | Passenger-oriented trial activity (**eVTOL** = electric vertical take-off and landing) |
| Infrastructure and vertiports | Sites, docking, planned logistics clusters (**vertiport** = industry word for a take-off/landing site) |
| Enabling technology | UTM, connectivity, shared platforms (**UTM** = unmanned aircraft system traffic management) |
| Insurance and finance | Risk transfer and capital products |
| Tangible services | Hands-on flight / MRO / patrol services (**MRO** = maintenance, repair, and overhaul) |
| Intangible services | Training, research, software-heavy services |

Use the map and sector lists on [Companies & sectors](landscape.qmd) for who appears where. This page does not repeat firm names.
